title: THE SAME PORTION, THE SAME ALTAR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'From what you offer you are to present this food offering to the LORD: the internal organs and all the fat that is connected to them, both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which you will remove with the kidneys.'" - Lev 3:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is now the third time in one chapter that these same organs have been listed. Cattle, sheep, goat — the same parts, described in the same words.

Repetition in Scripture is rarely accidental. God is pressing something into Israel's memory: what belongs to Me does not change based on what you can afford.

The poorest goat-owner gave God exactly what the wealthy cattle-owner gave — the fat, the kidneys, the inner parts. Proportionally, he gave the same. God asked no less of the poor and no more of the rich.

There is real dignity in this. God did not create a system where the poor worshipper was a spectator at somebody else's religion. His goat, his hand, his portion, his place at the meal.

And it protects the wealthy from a dangerous illusion too — that a larger gift buys a larger share of God. It does not. Paul warned Timothy to instruct the rich not to put their hope in wealth, which is so uncertain, but in God (1 Tim 6:17).

Before the altar, the categories that divide us in the world simply do not apply.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I unconsciously rank people spiritually by what they can contribute?
2. Am I giving God the same proportion of my inner life, whatever my outward circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, level my heart before Your altar. Let me neither despise the small offering nor be impressed by the large one. Amen.
